subject: Lyra12B — elevated 5xx/timeouts: incident update and recovery
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@wholesome.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lyra12B — elevated 5xx/timeouts: incident update and mitigation

Hi Marta —

Thanks for flagging this. We’re seeing a spike in 5xx and timeout errors originating from the Lyra12B model fleet starting ~08:45 PDT and impacting a subset of long-context generation requests. We’re actively triaging and I wanted to share what we know and our immediate mitigation plan: 

- Impact: increased 5xxs and timeouts for long-sequence generation (>2048 tokens) and some streaming endpoints. Not all requests are affected.
- Current mitigations in flight: (1) roll forward a kernel workaround to reduce KV cache pressure on a small canary of hosts, (2) enable fallback routing to the lyra6b-compatible variant for requests exceeding 3s, (3) add stricter per-request token limits for new sessions.
- ETA for stabilization: we expect noticeable reduction in errors within 60–90 minutes for trafficked paths; full fleet stabilization will take longer as we validate canary hosts.

I’ve attached log snippets (ops-incident-lyra12b-log-snippets.txt) that show the earliest correlated errors. Can you confirm the API endpoints and usage patterns you saw affected (project id / route names) so we can prioritize?

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact on your end and will keep you updated at least hourly until stabilized.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marta Lopez <marta@wholesome.ai>

Subject: Re: Lyra12B — elevated 5xx/timeouts: incident update and mitigation

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the quick note.

We are seeing errors primarily on two routes: /v1/generate (project: wholesome-prod) and a streaming route /v1/stream-chat (project: wholesome-stream). The errors started around 08:50 PDT and affect both short bursts and longer sessions—timeouts around 3–7s and 502s for some requests. Our SRE reported elevated client timeouts and ticket volume from internal users.

We’ll pause a few lower-priority batch jobs you mentioned to reduce load. ETA-sensitive: can you let us know if you plan to do any rolling restarts or model swaps that might briefly increase latency? We’d like to warn our customers.

—Marta
Marta Lopez

On Fri, Jun 5, 2027 at 09:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Marta —
> 
> Thanks for flagging this. We’re seeing a spike in 5xx and timeout errors originating from the Lyra12B model fleet...

Marta — quick technical update from ops/infra: we observed rapid growth in KV cache evictions on Lyra12B hosts under long-context workloads, which is resulting in a memory-pressure path that throws a service-level 5xx in the attention kernel. Symptoms:
- elevated GC/alloc pressure on GPU host agents
- repeated KV cache misses leading to backend exceptions on long requests (>2048)

Immediate steps taken (09:30–09:45):
1) Canary kernel patch (limits on per-request KV prefetch) applied to 5% of hosts to validate no regression.
2) Traffic split rule added: requests with tokens >2048 are routed to lyra6b-compat for the next 30 minutes as a safety fallback; this route adds small accuracy variance but reduces timeouts.
3) Autoscaler thresholds adjusted to preferentially add dedicated capacity for long-tail queues.

Planned next actions (pending Canary validation):
- If canary is stable for 20–30m we’ll roll to 25% and continue to 100% over a controlled window.
- If canary shows regression, we’ll immediately roll back and expand fallback routing.

Impact to you: the rollback/roll-forward actions may cause brief additional latencies on ~3–8 hosts during the window; we’ll notify a 10–15m notice prior to any fleet-wide roll.

I’ll keep monitoring and post another update when we see canary metrics.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Lyra12B — stabilization confirmed and next steps (postmortem draft attached)

Hi Marta —

Follow-up and recovery summary: the canary rollout we described stabilized after the kernel patch and routing change. We completed a controlled roll to 100% of Lyra12B hosts by 11:30 PDT on 6 Jun. Error rates returned to baseline and client timeouts dropped to pre-incident levels.

Root cause (brief): a combination of a memory leak in the KV cache path exposed by long-context workloads and a regression in a recent attention-optimizer kernel that increased transient alloc pressure. Under heavy long-tail sequences the hosts would exceed a threshold that produced an unhandled exception leading to 5xxs/timeouts.

What we did
- short term: kernel patch to limit aggressive prefetch + fallback routing to lyra6b-compat while patch validated
- medium term: patched memory leak in KV cache and rolled a combined release; added additional unit coverage for long-context paths
- long term: telemetry improvements (per-request KV usage metrics), tighter pre-deployment perf gates, and an automatic fallback policy for long-sequence requests during anomalous memory pressure

We attached a draft postmortem (postmortem-draft-lyra12b.pdf). Next steps from our side: final postmortem by 2027-06-10 and an offer of a one-time service credit for impacted usage; I’ll coordinate the formal credit proposal with billing and legal and follow up.

Please reply if you want a technical call to walk through the fix and mitigation; otherwise we’ll send the final postmortem and the credit paperwork next week.

Sincerely,
Naomi
